purpose: What happens to pressure when the same gas has more room?
meaning: Multiply the amount and gas constant by kelvin temperature, then divide by volume in litres to obtain kilopascals.

definition.setting: A sealed piston contains one mole of an ideal gas. Set its volume and temperature, then calculate its pressure. Increasing the available volume at the same temperature lowers the pressure; changing temperature changes the numerator as well. The drawing represents an equilibrium state, not a real-time piston experiment.

signature.result: The primary reported quantity in kPa.

conditions: One mole of ideal gas with R=8.31446261815324 L·kPa/(mol·K). Temperature uses kelvins. This dilute-gas model omits molecular volume and interactions; it does not model a compression path or heat transfer.
Inputs stay inside the declared control ranges. Each result uses the same parameter state in the story, formula and both views.
